items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: And John Morrell, Simon Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, Eddie Morrell, all musicians.

ctx.x: You can tell a little bit how they're related.

Related. Well, Milly Barnes and Paul Barnes, their mother was my father's sister. And John Morrell, Simon Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, Eddie Morrell, all musicians. Their mother was my father's sister from the Fraser.
Their mother was the Fraser. And the Barnes' mother was the Fraser.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: and we had, let's see, John, you see, was playing banjo with John Robeshoe.

ctx.x: Who was in that at that time?

Let's see, John Robeshoe Band, we had, let's see, now we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano, and we had, let's see, John, you see, was playing banjo with John Robeshoe. And then we had, sometimes Willie Paglia was to play trumpet. Uh-huh. And we had, uh, Charlie Love, John Robeshoe, himself on the band, on the violin, and Harrison Bones on trombone. Oh, yeah. I was on the drum, I'm thinking we played banjo, John, care banjo player sometimes. You…

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: Well, that same year you're speaking about was John Morrell had got several fellas out there in the tuxedo band to make that record.

ctx.x: That was the Young Morgan Band. Well, they called it Sam Morgan Band. Sam Morgan Band. Sam Morgan Band. But, say, Sammy got the best go year. You know, Johnny Day, I picked him right now, standing on Seminole in Claiborne waiting to catch the North Claiborne called the Ride Up Canal Street. Yeah. Well, that same year you're speaking about was John Morrell had got several fellas out there in the tuxedo band to make that record. I see. And he had wanted, Chani Bebe was the drummer, you see, but he was a crack…
So Paul Barch wasn't doing that band anymore then? Who? Paul Barch was gone. Oh no, no. He was up in New York that time.
